$comment: zenwatch.v1 (#614, FL3), Rust-first: what zenwatch's structs (zenwatch/src/publish.rs) and the fleet's doctor report (zenkey-fleet/src/report/doctor.rs) derive through schemars, committed. zenwatch's check_schema tests keep each top-level type in step with this file; descriptions are the structs' doc comments, their rustdoc links spelled as code.

CheckId.description: A check of zk2's doctor, by its stable id: an open vocabulary, since new checks append (`CheckId::ALL` lists them). A reader shows an id it does not know as written.

CheckReport.description:
One check's verdict (tooling guide §1): `Established` when it found
something, `NotEstablished` with the evidence of a clean answer,
`Unobservable` when a subject it had to decide could not be read, and
`NotAsked` when the run was not to ask it.

section.description: The core section the check enforces.

verdict.description: The check's question answered: the finding is the yes.

DisciplineCounters.description:
What the discipline did, counted (RFC 13 §3 O6: every bound reports
its cost, and every suppression is a number somewhere). Published in
`zenwatch.v1`'s `counters` (#614, FL3).

baseline.description: A first-observation `ok` — a baseline, not news.

cancelled.description: A `for` wait that returned to `ok` before it was announced.

deduped.description: Same identity, state and severity again.

evicted.description: Identities evicted at the bound, over the ledger's life.

grouped.description: Notices folded into a group (members, not groups).

sent.description: Notifications handed out for delivery (a group counts once).

clocks_synced.description:
Whether the run took the deployment's word that this host's clock
and the owners' agree (`--clocks-synced`, `freshness.v1` §2.6).
Without it, a reply's age is unobservable, and so are the checks that
conclude from a fresh document.

readings.description:
How many readings were taken: two, a grace apart, when
`config-projection` was asked; one otherwise.

selector.description: The selector the readings' GETs went out on, base-relative.

DoctorDelta.description:
What one doctor run says relative to the previous one (#389): findings
keyed on `(check, subject)`, so evidence and severity drift count as
unchanged. Computed by `crate::doctor_delta`; routed by a notifier's
scheduled doctor.

fixed.description: Findings present in the previous run and gone now.

new.description: Findings present now and absent from the previous run.

DoctorFinding.description:
One finding: what fired, on what, and the evidence.

`(check, subject)` is the finding's identity: `crate::doctor_delta`
compares runs on it, so a subject is spelled the same way every run —
`<system>/<service>@<instance>`, `<system>/<service> <role>`,
`<iface> <fingerprint>`, `<storage>@<zid>`.

evidence.description: What was observed, for a person.

clocks_synced.description:
Whether the run took the deployment's word that this host's clock
and the owners' agree (`--clocks-synced`, `freshness.v1` §2.6).
Without it, the doctor measures no clock, and a status reply's age is
unobservable.

selector.description: The selector both readings' GETs went out on, base-relative.

DoctorOutcome.description: `ok` or `failed`: whether a scheduled doctor run happened.

complete.description:
Whether every presence read ended at the routers' final reply. A
read that ended at its timeout may have missed tokens (§8.1).

grace_s.description: How far apart the two reads split-brain compares were taken.

revisions.description: Revisions the descriptors name, and how many of them are held.

undescribed.description: Instances whose descriptor was asked for and did not read.

DoctorReport.description:
zk2's doctor report: one `CheckReport` per check, in
`CheckId::ALL` order, and the scope they were judged over.

unobservable.description:
Set when presence showed no zk2 token at all — the empty scope —
with what was read. Every check that reads presence is then
unobservable, and the run is no verdict however clean the rest:
a doctor pointed at the wrong namespace must not be green.

DoctorScope.description: What one doctor run read: the scope that makes its silences legible.

config.description:
What the `config.v1` checks read (#768, CC). Absent when none was
asked.

health.description:
What the `health.v1` checks read (#721, PF). Absent when none was
asked.

namespace.description: The deployment's namespace; empty for the bus root.

presence.description:
The presence selector, base-relative in the namespace. Absent when
no check that reads presence was asked.

routers.description:
Routers that answered the admin space (`@/*/router`), read in no
namespace. Absent when no check that reads it was asked.

DoctorSeverity.description:
How bad a finding is: the ladder a `--fail-on` floor reads.

Shared with `field`'s findings (`crate::report::FieldFinding`).

oneOf.description:
A rule broken: a MUST or MUST NOT of the core, or the deployment
disagreeing with itself.

A SHOULD unmet, or a change a human has to accept: judgement is
degraded, not wrong.

FiringRule.description: `state/firing/{rule_id}`: what one rule currently has announced.

count.description:
How many notice identities are announced under this rule, this
one included.

id.description: The notice identity named here: the most severe, then the oldest.

since.description: RFC 3339: when the named notice's condition began.

Judgement.description:
One question's judgement — the four-pole core every tool verdict maps
onto (RFC 13, v1.24; RFC 09 §5.1 pre-v1.24). See the module doc.

oneOf.description:
Established(yes): the question was put and the claim holds — positive
evidence, conclusive.

Established(no): the question was put and the claim conclusively does
not hold — with the reason, which is where the honesty lives.

Unestablished: the question was not put — the input was not fetched,
was not requested, or does not exist for this subject. Not asked is
not answered no (RFC 09 §5.1 O4).

Unestablished: the question was put and the observation cannot carry
the claim — a drop under a completeness claim, a window shorter than
the claim's span, or an ask that failed (RFC 09 §5.1 O6).

Unjudged.description: A subject a check could not decide, and what stood in the way.

ZenwatchCounters.description:
`state/counters`: what the daemon did, and what its bounds cost, since
it started (RFC 13 §3 O6: every bound reports its cost).

delivered.description: Deliveries that went out, one per sink a notification reached.

dropped.description: Liveliness events the presence and token observers dropped.

firing_refused.description:
`firing/{rule_id}` documents the runtime refused at the bound
(core §2.7): once each time a rule's document became refused.

forgotten.description: Address records the presence projection forgot at its bound.

started_at.description: RFC 3339: when this run started; every count is since then.

state_entries.description: Entries the discipline's ledger holds now.

ZenwatchDoctor.description:
`state/doctor`: the scheduled doctor's last run (#390,
`crate::doctor`). Published after every run, successful or not.

delta.description:
The `DoctorDelta` against the previous run; absent on the baseline
and after a failed run.

error.description: Why a `failed` run could not happen.

findings.description: Findings in `report` — after a failed run, the retained report's.

fixed.description: Findings gone since the previous run.

new.description: Findings new since the previous run (`0` on the baseline).

next_at.description: RFC 3339: when the next one is due. In the past: the schedule lapsed.

ran_at.description: RFC 3339: when this run happened (or was attempted).

report.description:
The `DoctorReport`, exactly as `zenctl doctor --format json` prints
it: each check's verdict in the judgement shape, what was not asked
absent (RFC 13 §1). After a failed run, the last report that
succeeded, retained; `null` when none has yet. Carried as the value
it serialized to; its schema is the fleet's (`report::doctor`).

report_at.description:
RFC 3339: the run that produced `report` — `ran_at` on a successful
run, older after a failed one, absent when there is no report.
